Smoke test passes end-to-end: register/update/close/forget/list/get all work, JWT manager-id auto-detect resolved this session correctly, and the JSONL state log is clean.

## What I built

**`/manage`** at `/Users/claudio1/.claude/skills/manage/`:

- **`SKILL.md`** — the manager playbook with five plays (**plan**, **dispatch**, **status**, **check**, **close**, plus **forget** and a **Receiving a worker report** routing rule).
- **`scripts/workers.sh`** — per-manager JSONL state log at `~/.ai-harness/manager/<manager_cse_id>.jsonl`, auto-keyed by my own `cse_*` from the JWT. Subcommands: `register / update / close / forget / list [--all|--json] / get / path`.

## How it composes

- **Spawn**: `python3 -m remote_control new-session --dir <repo> --prompt-file <brief>` — auto-detects my `cse_*` and injects the reply-to header + env var so workers know where to reply.
- **Talk to worker**: `python3 -m remote_control sessions submit cse_<worker> --stdin` (confirm + dry-run + send, per `[[send-to-session]]`'s rule).
- **Receive from worker**: their reply lands here as a user turn with `[from cse_<worker> — reply via send-to-session]` — playbook explicitly says recognize the header and route to "Receiving a worker report" (record + surface verbatim to you + ask next action) rather than treat as a new request.
- **Close**: I instruct the worker to `/close-work` only after you OK; the worker handles its own review/merge/push/lease release/ticket close.

## Design choices per your answers

- **Skill name**: `/manage`.
- **Dispatch default**: file the GitHub ticket first on the right board (per `~/dev/GITHUB_PROJECTS.md`), have the worker `/start-work` to claim it. Raw prompt only for trivial one-shots you wave off.
- **Done handshake**: always send an explicit status-request before declaring done; surface the worker's reply verbatim; wait for your OK before instructing `/close-work`.
